The function $f(x)$ is defined and differentiable on $[-4,5].$ The graph of ${f}^{′}(x),$ the derivative of $f(x),$ is shown above. Find the minimum value of the function $f(x)$ on the interval $[-4,5]$ given that $f(-4)=-6.5.$
questions.worked_solution:
According to the candidates test, the minimum value of $f(x)$ on $[-4,5]$ must occur at a critical point or an endpoint of the interval. 

**Step 1**: Find the critical points:

We see that ${f}^{′}(x)$ is defined everywhere on $x\in (-4,5),$ and ${f}^{′}(x)=0$ at $x=-3,-1.$ Therefore, the candidates are $x=-4,-3,-1,5.$

**Step 2**: Compute the values of $f$ for each candidate using the fundamental theorem of calculus:

The function is made up of $3$ triangles and $2$ trapezoid. Let's add the areas bounded by these shapes to our diagram:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14274266/assets/68c662c352368133cd27c4f99313c055d9466351ab4f62ac58acc7873277bf6a.png)

Using the given information and the fundamental theorem of calculus, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-4) & =-6.5 \\ f(-3) & =f(-4)+{\int }_{-4}^{-3}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-6.5+0.5 \\  & =-6 \\ f(-1) & =f(-4)+{\int }_{-4}^{1}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-6.5+0.5+(-1) \\  & =-7 \\ f(5) & =f(-4)+{\int }_{-4}^{5}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-6.5+0.5+(-1)+2+3+3 \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**:  Select the smallest value of $f$ from our candidates.

Comparing the values of $f$ found in step $2,$ we have

$$
{f}_{\text{min}}=min\{-6.5,-6,-7,1\}=-7.
$$

Therefore, the minimum value of $f$ is ${f}_{\text{min}}=-7,$ and the value of $x$ that minimizes $f(x)$ is ${x}_{\text{min}}=-1.$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-4) & =3 \\ f(-1) & =f(-4)+{\int }_{-4}^{-1}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =3-2 \\  & =1 \\ f(2) & =f(-4)+{\int }_{-4}^{2}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =3-2+5 \\  & =6 \\ f(5) & =f(-4)+{\int }_{-4}^{5}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =3-2+5-9 \\  & =-3\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Select the smallest value of $f$ from our candidates.

Comparing the values of $f$ found in step $2,$ we have 

$$
{f}_{\text{min}}=min\{3,1,6,-3\}=-3.
$$

Therefore, the minimum value of $f$ is ${f}_{\text{min}}=-3,$ and the value of $x$ that minimizes $f(x)$ is ${x}_{\text{min}}=5.$

$$
{h}_{\text{min}}=min\{-1,3,3,1\}=-1.
